links.targetTitle: SPK emissions beyond the 10 billion Genesis Supply are perma

title: Sky Governance retains the sole override on SPK's emissions cap, and only to enforce Risk Capital requirements
content:
The same provision that makes SPK's supply cap irreversible for Spark Governance immediately carves out an exception: per A.6.1.1.1.2.1.4.2.1.1.6, "Sky Governance retains the ability to revert where Spark is in violation of Risk Capital requirements and emissions are required by the Risk Framework" (see A.3.2 - Risk Capital).

Read against the preceding sentence, "permanently disabled" is a statement about **who** cannot revert it, not about whether it can be reverted at all. The two clauses look contradictory but resolve into a deliberate asymmetry: the Agent cannot dilute its own holders for its own convenience; the parent ecosystem can dilute them to recapitalize the Agent.

That asymmetry is what makes the arrangement an enforcement mechanism rather than a loophole. SPK holders are the residual risk-bearers of Spark's balance sheet: if Spark operates outside the Risk Framework and needs capital, the token supply is where that capital comes from. Dilution becomes the penalty attached to risk violations, and it lands on exactly the constituency that benefited from taking the risk.

The consequence for holders is that SPK's fixed supply is conditional on Spark's ongoing compliance with the Risk Framework — a fact that is easy to miss if only the first half of the provision is read.
description: The permanence of the cap is asymmetric: the parent ecosystem can re-enable minting when Spark violates the Risk Framework, turning dilution into an enforcement instrument.
